title: Week 1 Networking — Doubt-Solving Session
session_goals: Collect week-one feedback from the cohort and clarify course logistics (capstone, labs, API keys)
Walk through the most upvoted week-one doubts one by one (transformer internals: Q/K/V, embeddings, FFN, KV cache)
Answer career-shaped questions: depth needed for AI-engineering roles, recruiter signals, and how image models relate to LLMs

questions.summary: Hands-on math example with a 10-token vocabulary: step-by-step walkthrough of next-token prediction, attention, and FFN.
questions.answer_summary: Worked examples exist in the cohort notes (BERT-style attention visualiser). One-on-one walkthrough in the chat if needed.

questions.summary: Is the encoder only used during training, or also at inference? When is the encoder needed?
questions.answer_summary: Modern (GPT-style) LLMs are decoder-only — no encoder at all. Encoder-only (BERT) is used for embedding models in RAG. Encoder-decoder (Vaswani 2017) uses encoder for K/V at every call (training or inference).

questions.summary: Where are embedding vectors physically stored? What is the 'clustering' mechanism? Is it a vector DB?
questions.answer_summary: Embeddings live inside the model weights as rows of the |V| × D matrix. Not in a separate DB at inference time. The vector-DB association comes from RAG (a separate concept).

questions.summary: Why 768 dimensions? How is the dimension chosen, and how are individual embedding values computed?
questions.answer_summary: D is an architectural hyperparameter (768 / 1024 / 4096 / 8192). Float values come from random init + gradient descent; frozen after pre-training.

questions.summary: When a token is wrongly predicted, backprop updates Q/K/V. Does it also update the token-to-vector mapping (embeddings)?
questions.answer_summary: Backprop updates everything learnable — embeddings, Q/K/V, FFN. The distinction is learnable (weights) vs not-learnable (tokenizer rules). Position embeddings can be fixed or learnable by design.

questions.summary: If a token wasn't in training, does the model learn it, decompose it, or hallucinate?
questions.answer_summary: The model cannot learn at inference. BPE tokenizers decompose into known subwords; the LLM makes best-guess answers = hallucination. RAG and fine-tuning reduce but don't eliminate.

questions.summary: How are Q, K, V computed from the input embedding matrix? How is the projection matrix W derived?
questions.answer_summary: Q, K, V = X · W_Q, X · W_K, X · W_V. The W matrices are learnable (random init, trained by gradient descent). Math is in the cohort notes.

questions.summary: Is KV cache the same as QKV, or something different? Will it be covered later?
questions.answer_summary: KV cache holds previously-computed K, V across generation steps. Q is recomputed each step. Same K/V from the attention computation, cached for efficiency.

questions.summary: FFN transforms to more 'relatable' dimensions. How are those dimensions calculated?
questions.answer_summary: FFN expands D to 4D (typical), applies non-linear activation, projects back to D. 4× is a design heuristic from Vaswani 2017; not derived from first principles.

questions.summary: Will completing the cohort enable applying for Forward-Deployed Engineer roles, or only contribute to internal projects?
questions.answer_summary: Both. Fundamentals cover both interview readiness and production system-building. Past cohorts produced both job-switchers and internal-project builders.

questions.summary: Will EVAL coverage be low-level example or high-level explanation? Will it cover RAG and agent fine-tuning?
questions.answer_summary: Architecturally agnostic, metric-driven. Specific metrics for RAG, agents, multi-agents — applicable regardless of underlying stack.

questions.summary: What signals should I create to get noticed by AI recruiters, and which platform to use?
questions.answer_summary: Personal brand via published artifacts (blogs, open-source repos) is the highest-leverage signal. Specific platform matters less than connecting with the right people.

questions.topic: Transformer depth needed for AI engineers
questions.summary: How much transformer depth do AI engineers need? Do teams implement this in production (agents, RAG)?
questions.answer_summary: Basic attention understanding is beyond what's required. Production AI engineering is mostly system-building around API LLMs (RAG, agents, evals, orchestration). Multi-agents are emerging but not widely deployed.

questions.summary: When OpenAI upgrades GPT-3.5 → GPT-5, do they train from scratch or extend?
questions.answer_summary: Labs do not retrain from scratch (cost prohibitive). They run a post-training cycle (SFT + preference opt) on new data. Pre-training = language; post-training = conversation / instruction-following.

questions.summary: Are post-training and validation the same thing?
questions.answer_summary: No. Validation = held-out data split. Post-training = second training stage (SFT + preference opt). Different concepts at different pipeline stages.

questions.summary: Is Spark used to orchestrate model training? How does that relate to training infra?
questions.answer_summary: Two types of orchestration: (1) data pre-processing — Spark/Beam/Ray for scraping/curing/PII-stripping; (2) GPU / training orchestration — distributing a single training run across thousands of GPUs (its own full topic).

questions.summary: How similar are diffusion models (ComfyUI) to LLMs? Is attention the same? Can we mix components like DeepSeek tokenizer + Gemma attention?
questions.answer_summary: Same transformer backbone + attention. Differ in inputs (text vs image latents) and outputs (next-token vs denoise). LoRA works for both but with different mechanics. Mixing tokenizer + attention across models does not work — embeddings are aligned with K/V.

questions.topic: How LLMs adapt to preferences at inference
questions.summary: When an LLM complies with 'don't use emojis' mid-conversation, is something being penalised under the hood?
questions.answer_summary: No inference-time fine-tuning. Either: (1) it's an agent with external memory (CLAUDE.md, project skills) re-injected every call, or (2) prior chat messages stay in context window.

questions.summary: Best way to connect the dots from the week-1 lectures into a single mind-map?
questions.answer_summary: Curated resources → structured prompt to Claude (or similar) → 2-3 iteration cycles → tighten sections. Excalidraw MCP for visual diagrams.

concepts.name: Transformer architecture (encoder-only vs decoder-only vs encoder-decoder)
concepts.definition: The transformer is the backbone of all modern LLMs. Modern LLMs use only the decoder half; encoder-only models like BERT are used for embeddings; the original encoder-decoder was designed for sequence-to-sequence tasks like machine translation.

concepts.name: Embeddings storage (weights vs vector DB)
concepts.definition: LLM embeddings live inside the model weights as rows of a |V| × D matrix — not in a separate vector DB. Vector DBs are a separate concept used in RAG to store external document embeddings.

concepts.name: Embedding dimension D (hyperparameter)
concepts.definition: The hidden dimension D (e.g. 768, 1024, 4096, 8192) is an architectural choice set at design time. It dominates the parameter count of the embedding table and FFN expansion.

concepts.name: Feed-forward network (D → 4D → D)
concepts.definition: The FFN block expands the embedding dimension by 4×, applies a non-linear activation (ReLU/SwiGLU), then projects back to D. Activation is what gives FFN representational power.

concepts.name: Q, K, V from input via learned projections
concepts.definition: Q, K, V are linear projections Q = X·W_Q, K = X·W_K, V = X·W_V. The W matrices are learnable parameters, randomly initialized and trained by gradient descent.

concepts.name: KV cache as inference optimization
concepts.definition: The KV cache stores the K and V tensors computed for prior tokens across generation steps. Q is recomputed each step. Without the cache, each new token would re-encode all prior tokens.

concepts.name: Learnable vs frozen parameters in training
concepts.definition: During training backprop updates all learnable parameters (weights, biases, embeddings, Q/K/V matrices). Tokenizer rules (BPE merges, token-ID mapping) are computed once and frozen.

concepts.name: Hallucination via BPE decomposition
concepts.definition: When an unknown word is given at inference, the BPE tokenizer decomposes it into known subwords. The LLM produces a best-guess answer = hallucination. Reduced by RAG (more context), fine-tuning (baked corrections), or tool calling (external lookup).

concepts.name: Pre-training vs post-training
concepts.definition: Pre-training = next-token prediction on huge corpus. Post-training = SFT (instruction-following) + preference optimization (RLHF/DPO/GRPO). Both update weights; both are training.

concepts.name: Validation = held-out data split, NOT post-training
concepts.definition: Validation is the practice of holding out a fraction of training data (10-20%) to estimate generalization. It is not a separate training phase.

concepts.name: Inference is not a training phase
concepts.definition: Inference is a forward pass through a frozen model. Post-training is a separate training phase. Models do not learn at inference; agent layers (memory, skills, RAG) feed context but do not modify model weights.

concepts.name: Two kinds of orchestration
concepts.definition: Data orchestration (Spark/Beam) for pre-training data pipeline. GPU orchestration (Megatron, GPipe) for distributing a single training run across many GPUs.

concepts.name: Diffusion models share transformer backbone with LLMs
concepts.definition: Image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, Flux) use the same transformer + attention architecture as LLMs. Inputs are image patches or VAE latents instead of text tokens; outputs are iteratively-denoised images instead of next-token.

concepts.name: LoRA for LLMs and image models
concepts.definition: LoRA (low-rank adaptation) is a technique to fine-tune a frozen base model by training a small adapter. Used in diffusion for character/style LoRAs; used in LLMs for domain fine-tuning. Different mechanics per modality.

concepts.name: Evals as metric-driven QA
concepts.definition: Modern evaluation suites (RAGAS, DeepEval, Phoenix) define specific metrics: faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision/recall, tool-call accuracy. Stack-agnostic.

concepts.name: Career signals for AI engineers
concepts.definition: Highest-leverage recruiter signals are personal brand via published artifacts (weekly blog posts distilling learnings, open-source repos with thoughtful READMEs), not any specific platform.

concepts.name: AI engineering depth calibration
concepts.definition: For most AI engineering roles, system-level depth (RAG, agents, evals, orchestration around an API-hosted LLM) matters more than frontier-lab ML depth (rewriting attention math, training from scratch).

concepts.name: Agents maintain external memory
concepts.definition: Modern LLM apps (ChatGPT, Claude) are agent systems with external memory (CLAUDE.md, project skills, user-level preferences) that re-feed context on every call. Not 'learning at inference' — application-layer memory.

qa_themes.theme: Encoder vs decoder at inference (modern LLMs are decoder-only)
qa_themes.answer: Encoder-decoder was for original transformer; modern LLMs only use the decoder; encoder-only used for embeddings in RAG.

qa_themes.theme: Embeddings are weights, not a vector DB
qa_themes.answer: They are rows of the |V| × D matrix inside the model weights. Vector DB confusion comes from RAG (a separate concept).

qa_themes.theme: Backprop updates everything learnable, including embeddings
qa_themes.answer: Embeddings, Q/K/V, FFN are all updated; tokenizer rules are frozen.

qa_themes.theme: KV cache is a per-step optimization caching K, V
qa_themes.answer: Q is recomputed each step; K and V are cached from prior steps to avoid re-encoding.
BPE decomposes unknown words; LLM synthesizes an answer from known sub-pieces; this is structurally hallucination.
Pre-training teaches language; post-training teaches conversation/instruction-following; validation is a held-out data split, NOT a training phase.
System-level depth (RAG/agents/evals) > transformer internals depth for AI-engineering roles. Portfolio artifacts are the highest-leverage recruiter signal.

qa_themes.theme: Diffusion models and LLMs are architectural cousins
qa_themes.answer: Same transformer backbone; differ in modality (image vs text) and output (denoise vs next-token). LoRA works for both but differently.

key_takeaways: Modern LLMs are decoder-only; encoder-only lives on as embedding backbones for RAG.
Embeddings live inside model weights, NOT in a vector DB (vector-DB confusion comes from RAG).
Backprop updates everything learnable: embeddings, Q/K/V, FFN. Tokenizer rules are not learnable.
KV cache ≠ QKV. It is an inference-time optimization caching K/V across generation steps.
Hallucination is structural, not a bug: BPE + best-guess + no real-time learning.
Pre-training + post-training are both training. Validation is a held-out data split, not a training phase.
For AI engineering roles, system-level depth (RAG, agents, evals) > transformer internals depth.
Personal brand via published artifacts (blogs, open-source repos) is the highest-leverage recruiter signal.
Diffusion models and LLMs share the transformer backbone; difference is modality.
Cannot fine-tune at inference — anything that 'remembers' preferences is an agent layer feeding context.
